q1: SELECT DISTINCT VIEWER_ID AS ID FROM VIEWS GROUP BY VIEW_DATE, VIEWER_ID HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT ARTICLE_ID) > 1 ORDER BY ID
q2: SELECT DISTINCT VIEWER_ID AS ID FROM VIEWS GROUP BY VIEWER_ID, VIEW_DATE HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT(ARTICLE_ID)) >= 2
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT DISTINCT VIEWER_ID AS ID FROM VIEWS GROUP BY VIEW_DATE, VIEWER_ID HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT ARTICLE_ID) > 1 ORDER BY ID
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT DISTINCT VIEWER_ID AS ID FROM VIEWS GROUP BY VIEWER_ID, VIEW_DATE HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT(ARTICLE_ID)) >= 2
counterexample: INSERT INTO VIEWS (ARTICLE_ID, AUTHOR_ID, VIEWER_ID, VIEW_DATE) VALUES (1, 101, 201, '2023-01-01'); INSERT INTO VIEWS (ARTICLE_ID, AUTHOR_ID, VIEWER_ID, VIEW_DATE) VALUES (2, 102, 201, '2023-01-01');
explanation: Q1 groups by VIEW_DATE and VIEWER_ID, requiring that the viewer viewed more than one distinct article on the same date. Q2 groups by VIEWER_ID and VIEW_DATE, requiring that the viewer viewed at least two distinct articles on the same date, regardless of the order of viewing.
counterexample_dsp: A viewer views two different articles on the same date. Q1 will not return this viewer as it requires the articles to be viewed on the same date, while Q2 will return this viewer as it only requires the articles to be viewed on the same date.
